# Unit 3 week 5 — Explained answers
A: Equipment defines the type; camera/tripod refer to instances. __init__ initialises a created instance and returns None; self identifies the receiving instance. total is a parameter, self._total is stored instance state. Worked output E01 2; True 1; False 1; True 2; E02 1.
B: zero stock permits construction but lend(1) returns False. A two-unit item lend(2)=>True/available 0; lend(1)=>False/unchanged; return_units(2)=>True/available 2; repeated return=>False/unchanged. Positive integer quantities only; invalid zero/negative/string/bool raise ValueError before changes. Empty/whitespace/non-string ID/name and invalid total are rejected. Queries do not change state.
C: underscore does not enforce privacy. A direct edit can break the invariant. Separate constructions have independent state; aliases share identity. A class-level events list is shared; an instance list initialised in __init__ is independent. Refactoring groups per-item data and operations; catalogue uniqueness, input/output and real borrower/date logic remain outside this small stock model.
D: solution includes linear lookup and report. Missing/empty lookup=>None; empty report=>[]. A found instance aliases the catalogue item, so lend changes it. A report contains strings/integers in new dictionaries and is a snapshot: an old report retains its earlier availability while a newly generated one reflects current state. Unique ID checking is the catalogue's responsibility.
Review state design, method contracts, independence/alias explanations, edge-test evidence and behavioural equivalence with the procedural version. Use this as optional, ungraded practice. Inheritance/polymorphism follow in week 6.
